business.description: Revathi Equipment India Limited (REIL) manufactures blast hole drills and exploratory drills for construction and mining applications as well as water well drills. The Company's revenue is derived principally from the sale of drills and spares, supported by maintenance and after-sales service.

outlook.statement: After a subdued year, your Company expects order inflow and revenues to improve in the next financial year.

Emerging markets in Africa, Asia and South America remain substantially untapped by the Company. Your Company has sufficient reserves and surplus to fund expansion in domestic and export markets, and a recovery in order inflow would improve capacity utilisation, absorption of fixed cost and operating margin.

Developing excavator mounted drills, pneumatic drills, Top Hammer Drills, roto moulded plastic tanks for weight optimisation, platform standardisation on C625D DTH & Top hammer Jackless products, deployment of Autonomous Drill on all exports, conceptual design & development of EV (Electric Vehicle) Drills for C750E rotary, deployment of product upgrades towards improving product availability >95%

orders_or_contracts.statement: Order intake during the year was significantly below expectations.
Took up a drilling contract in a key market wherein the customer pays per meter drilled.

risks: Customer concentration - significant portion of revenue derived from limited number of customers
Working capital and receivables - long manufacturing cycles and high-value inventory make business working capital intensive
Corporate guarantee provided for promoter group company's credit facilities - potential invocation risk

Quality, warranty and product liability risks
New product development delays or lower market acceptance
Single manufacturing location at Coimbatore exposing to regional natural disasters, state policy changes, political/civil disruption
Energy transition - Investment in renewable/nuclear generation under SHANTI Act, 2025 may gradually reduce coal demand beyond 2035
Customer financing - higher interest rates or reduced credit availability may reduce sales
External conditions - economic/political conditions, inflation, interest/exchange rates, commodity price volatility, taxation/regulation changes, force majeure events
Cybersecurity risk from vulnerabilities in IT systems and networks
Regulatory risk from new Labour Codes implementation
Credit rating downgrade risk for bank facilities
Technology absorption not fully completed for imported autonomous drill kits and smart controls
Dependency on imported technology for autonomous systems

The company does not face significant liquidity risk with regard to the lease liabilities as the current assets are sufficient to meet the obligations related to lease liabilities as and when they fall due.
